answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity on cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Validating an agent requires progressive stake commitments across network tier boundaries: an entry-tier copper staking requirement escalates across intermediate basalt validation clusters into high-assurance tundra security zones. Because staking demands scale as O(k^2) across concurrent identities, attackers face superlinear capital exhaustion, making massive Sybil swarms exponentially cost-prohibitive.
